clue.text: When without support I have to be harsh

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for when goes around the support

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
a bra is a supporting undergarment
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone resolves that, with no backing, they must turn harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: AS goes around BRA to give ABRAS, then I'VE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a manner that is rough and grating towards others.

clue.text: Animal found by an accountant at foot of mountain

indicators.note: in a down answer the following letters sit below the mountain, at its foot

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
an gives the article A
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An animal is found by an accountant at the base of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American relative of the llama, kept for its wool.

clue.text: Wave very gently when beset by bother

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the letters for very gently are enclosed by the word for bother

parts.note: to rile is to annoy or bother
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: Someone waves very gently while being pestered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset by' puts PP inside RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripple is a small wave on the surface of water.

clue.text: Peculiar little stone found on the mountains

parts.note: st is the short form of stone, the weight unit
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: An odd little stone is found up in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean odd or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Dithering, being unwell in the course of holiday

indicators.note: something happening in the course of a period falls within it, so the word goes inside

parts.note: vacation is a holiday
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates, feeling sick while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the course of' puts ILL inside VACATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Wavering indecisively between options.

clue.text: Sailor left with a mark after accident

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by an injury

explanation.surface: A seaman is left scarred after a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A lascar is a seaman from India or South-East Asia, historically serving on European ships.

clue.text: Pantomime character who speaks the opening words

definitions.text: Pantomime character who speaks the opening words

parts.words: Pantomime character who speaks the opening words
parts.note: opening words can mean words that make something open, like the magic phrase to the robbers' cave

explanation.surface: A stage figure who delivers a play's first lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show based on folk tales; this hero opens the cave with 'Open sesame'.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcutter of the Arabian Nights tale who says 'Open sesame' to open the thieves' cave.

clue.text: Girl entering taxi is providing drug

indicators.note: the girl goes into the taxi, so her name sits inside it

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl getting into a taxi is supplying narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts ANN inside CAB, giving CANNAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is a drug made from the hemp plant.

clue.text: Very hot enclosure around kiln

indicators.note: the enclosure goes around the kiln, holding it inside

parts.note: a ring is an enclosed area, as in a boxing ring
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: An enclosure around a kiln is extremely hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts RING around OAST. An oast is a kiln for drying hops, common in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasting describes heat so intense it feels like an oven.

clue.text: Will the churchwarden give this support? On the contrary

definitions.text: Will the churchwarden give this support? On the contrary

parts.words: Will the churchwarden give this support? On the contrary
parts.note: a churchwarden is also a long clay tobacco pipe, so the reversed question asks what holds up such pipes

explanation.surface: A question about whether a parish official will back some cause.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay pipe; 'on the contrary' flips the question, so it is this stand that supports the churchwarden.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand made to hold smoking pipes when not in use.

clue.text: When burnt brown, girl is somersaulting

indicators.note: a somersault turns head over heels, so the girl's name and the following word are read backwards together

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is tumbling head over heels while getting a tan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somersaulting' reverses ANNE IS as one run, giving SIENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt sienna is the name of a reddish-brown pigment made by roasting this earth.

clue.text: Pass giving entry to single officer

indicators.note: the pass lets the following word come in, so it is placed inside the mountain pass

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountains
lone means single or solitary

explanation.surface: A permit admits one officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving entry to' puts LONE inside COL. 'Pass' looks like a permit, but here it means a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army rank, above a lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: Countryman gets game bird — hard to miss

indicators.note: the bird goes without the letter for hard, so that letter is left out

parts.note: the pheasant is a common game bird
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A rural man bags a game bird, but finds it hard not to miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to miss' drops H from PHEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a small farmer or rural labourer, someone of the countryside.

clue.text: The cosmetically treated madam butterfly

explanation.surface: A heavily made-up brothel-keeper, plus an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madam butterfly' suggests the opera, but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman wearing heavy make-up, and a common orange-and-black migratory butterfly species.

clue.text: Anti regalia, somehow opposed to hierarchy

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone against royal trappings is, in some way, against rank too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters of ANTI REGALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An egalitarian believes all people are equal, rejecting ranked social orders.

clue.text: Queen unwell and failing in spirit

parts.note: Queen gives QU
ailing means unwell

explanation.surface: The queen is sick and losing heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Quailing means losing courage and shrinking back in fear.

clue.text: Fellow with weapon, eastern weapon, coming within range

indicators.note: the letters come inside the word for range, so they are placed within it

parts.note: span is a range or extent
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A man with a weapon, an eastern one, comes within shooting distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming within' puts E and ARM inside SPAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearman is a soldier armed with a lance-like pole weapon.

clue.text: A foreign boy to rampage, one more or less opposed to native land

parts.note: un is French for a
Pat is a boy's name
a riot is a violent rampage
I is the Roman numeral one
c, short for circa, means approximately

explanation.surface: A foreign lad on the rampage seems rather against his own country.
explanation.walkthrough: C stands for circa, Latin for about, used with uncertain dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disloyal or hostile to one's own country.

clue.text: Praise attempts almost overcoming objection

indicators.note: to overcome is to be on top of, so here the word for attempts surrounds the objection
almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: tries are attempts
a but is an objection, as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: Praise for efforts that nearly win over a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TRIES to TRIE; 'overcoming' wraps TRIE around BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is an expression of praise or honour.

clue.text: Fancy putting lid on food!

parts.note: a cap is a lid
rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the whim of covering a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'putting lid on' places CAP above RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a whim or sudden fancy.

clue.text: Girl among the best he remembered

indicators.note: among says the answer lies within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A girl among the finest he recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' signals the name inside bEST HE Remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a girl's name, also a queen in the Bible.

clue.text: Say, Dorothy's served up really solid food!

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
Dot is short for Dorothy, plus the possessive s

explanation.surface: Dorothy's dished up something very heavy to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses EG DOTS as one run, giving STODGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling food such as suet pudding.

clue.text: I hurried alongside man from middle eastern country

parts.note: ran means hurried
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone says they ran alongside a man from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a person or thing belonging to Iran, a Middle Eastern nation.

clue.text: Top side unlikely to be put down

indicators.note: an unlikely arrangement of the letters is not the one shown, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leading team is not expected to be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' rearranges TOP SIDE. 'put down' suggests defeat but means placed down.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something down or place it is to set it in a spot.

clue.text: Early in the morning almost broke foot

parts.note: 1 a.m. is early in the morning, with the 1 written as I

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: bust means broke, out of money

explanation.surface: In the small hours someone nearly broke a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the T of BUST. 1 a.m. becomes I AM by reading the figure 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An iambus is a metrical foot of one short and one long syllable.

clue.text: Showered in bathroom on island — building at bottom of garden?

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, a bathroom
a shed is the outbuilding typically at the end of a garden

explanation.surface: Someone took a shower in an island bathroom, perhaps in a garden outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: To lavish gifts is to heap them generously on someone, like a downpour.

clue.text: It's good to exasperate the foreman!

parts.note: to anger is to exasperate

explanation.surface: It's a fine thing to infuriate the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganger is the overseer of a gang of labourers.

clue.text: Where the last king's attendant stood indeed!

definitions.text: Where the last king's attendant stood

explanation.surface: A courtier's position beside the late monarch, and an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: The last British king was George VI, so his attendant stood beside him.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, beside the late monarch; also a dated exclamation of surprise or emphasis, like 'goodness!'.
